welcome:
Welcome to the tmux CLI Playground.
Type commands to explore a simulated terminal multiplexer.
Type 'help' for available commands, 'scenario' for guided labs.

scenarios.title: Set Up an Incident Response Workspace

steps.instruction: Create a new tmux session named 'incident-2026' for the ongoing incident.
Create a new window named 'logs' to tail application logs.
Split the current window horizontally to have logs on the left and a shell on the right.
Split the right pane vertically to add a metrics pane below.
List all panes to confirm the layout.
Create another window named 'comms' for incident communication.
List all windows to see the workspace layout.
Switch back to the logs window (window 1) to start monitoring.
List all existing tmux sessions to find the one you were disconnected from.
Reattach to the 'monitoring' session that was running your dashboards.
List windows to see what was running before the disconnect.
Switch to window 2 where your Grafana queries were running.
Display pane numbers to orient yourself in the split layout.
Enter copy mode to scroll back and see output you missed during disconnection.
Kill the stale 'deploy' session that is no longer needed.
Rename your current session to 'incident-2026' to reflect its new purpose.

commands.help:
Available commands:
  tmux new -s <name>             — Create a new named session
  tmux ls                        — List all sessions
  tmux attach -t <name>          — Attach to a session
  tmux kill-session -t <name>    — Kill a session
  tmux rename-session <name>     — Rename current session
  tmux switch -t <name>          — Switch to another session
  tmux new-window -n <name>      — Create a new window
  tmux list-windows              — List all windows
  tmux select-window -t <n>      — Switch to window N
  tmux rename-window <name>      — Rename current window
  tmux kill-window               — Kill current window
  tmux split-window -h           — Split pane horizontally
  tmux split-window -v           — Split pane vertically
  tmux select-pane -t <n>        — Select pane N
  tmux resize-pane -D <n>        — Resize pane down by N rows
  tmux list-panes                — List panes in current window
  tmux swap-pane                 — Swap panes
  tmux display-panes             — Show pane numbers
  tmux copy-mode                 — Enter scroll/copy mode
  tmux clock-mode                — Show clock in pane
  tmux show-options -g           — Show global options
  tmux set -g mouse on           — Enable mouse support
  tmux source-file ~/.tmux.conf  — Reload config
  tmux list-keys                 — List key bindings
  tmux info                      — Show server info
  tmux display-message           — Show status message
  tmux show-environment          — Show environment variables

  scenario                       — Start a guided lab
  clear                          — Clear the terminal
  help                           — Show this help
